key_bets: Confinement scaling from LDX's 14.5 ms to the required 3.5 s energy confinement time (~240× extrapolation) holds at Bohm-like or better behavior in a high-β levitated dipole
Q_sci = 15 operating point is achievable with 44.5 MW ICRH in a dipole field geometry where RF wave coupling has never been experimentally demonstrated
A single levitated REBCO coil at 23 T peak field with on-board superconducting flux pump and neon-slush cooling can be operated with periodic (annual) sacrificial-section replacement
TBR = 1.1 is achievable with natural (unenriched) Li₂O solid ceramic blanket covering only ~75% of neutron solid angle, relying on tungsten neutron multiplication
Tungsten W-B₄C-W radiatively-cooled shield tiles can operate steady-state at 1950 K (above recrystallization) under 14 MeV neutron flux for plant-relevant lifetimes
Annual docking/replacement of an activated internal HTS coil (~864 km/yr REBCO) can be performed economically with remote handling that has not yet been designed or costed
40% thermal efficiency is realized through an unspecified thermodynamic cycle (Rankine vs. sCO₂) on a tritium-bearing primary loop
eliminated_costs: Disruption mitigation systems, thermal dump resistors, and disruption-driven first-wall replacement — levitated dipole carries no plasma current and is mechanistically disruption-free
Thermal energy storage for grid decoupling during pulse transitions — plasma is inherently steady-state, with duty cycle set by cryogenic limits rather than pulse physics
Lithium-6 isotope enrichment infrastructure — TBR = 1.1 achieved with natural Li₂O via tungsten neutron multiplication
External toroidal field coils, poloidal field coils, and central solenoid — replaced by a single levitated internal coil
Precision steel vacuum vessel — outer vessel is reinforced concrete (38,700 t of 45,100 t total plant mass) using standard civil construction
novel_costs: Annual sacrificial coil replacement: ~864 km/yr of REBCO tape plus remote handling and qualification testing (~$52M/yr at baseline, ~30% of annual capital charge) — no analogue in any other fusion concept
Remote handling system for an activated, neutron-irradiated levitated HTS coil assembly including hot-cell refurbishment and spare-coil pool logistics (~$150M capex, undesigned)
On-board neon-slush cryogenic reservoir with rapid drain-and-refill docking system, exposed to neon supply-chain constraints (byproduct of air liquefaction, ~200,000 m³/year global)
Tritium accounting and inventory management during periodic docking cycles when the core magnet passes through the blanket region
On-board superconducting flux pump scaled to charge a ~20 GJ, 29.4 kA-operating-current levitated coil with no current leads

risks.description: Confinement scaling fails at Tahi (~2028): Bohm-like n·τ_e ≥ 3.23×10¹⁹ s·m⁻³ at 1 keV not achieved, making Reactor A nonviable as designed — a binary threshold with no intermediate 'more expensive but viable' outcome

Annual sacrificial coil replacement cost unquantified; at $75/kA-m REBCO, raw cost ~$47M/yr (~30% of annual capital charge), and LCOE uncertainty spans a factor of ~2 from this single parameter until costed
Absolute overnight capital and LCOE figures are withheld by OpenStar as 'preliminary and subject to change' — no company anchor point exists for TEA validation

ICRH coupling in dipole magnetic geometry has never been experimentally demonstrated; 44.5 MW heating at claimed 70% wall-plug efficiency in a topology fundamentally different from tokamaks is unverified

Plasma edge physics uncharacterized — edge temperature (800 eV) and pressure (10³ Pa) bounds borrowed from I-mode tokamak data with no dipole experimental basis; tighter limits would depress triple product, Q_sci, and net output
REBCO tape behavior at 23 T peak field, 30 K, under combined mechanical stress and 14 MeV neutron fluence to 1 MW-yr/m² is uncharacterized — irradiation database exists only to ~10–12 T
Thermal conversion cycle (Rankine vs. sCO₂ Brayton) unspecified; a 5-percentage-point efficiency shift (40% → 35%) lowers net output ~12% and raises LCOE proportionally

Tungsten tile shield creep and mechanical performance above 1950 K recrystallization under 14 MeV neutron irradiation is not demonstrated; structural integrity over plant lifetime relies on hope that 'other forms of damage dominate'

Li₂O solid ceramic blanket has not been tested at 14 MeV fluences and fusion-relevant temperatures; tritium inventory, permeation, and structural performance under thermal cycling and neutron swelling are unvalidated at scale

REBCO tape supply chain — global production of 1,000–2,000 km/year is insufficient for a single Reactor A build (~5,520 km) plus annual replacement (~864 km/yr), shared with competing HTS tokamak programs
Neon cryogen supply is limited (~200,000 m³/year global, air-separation byproduct); fleet-scale operation may require hydrogen fallback with 5× larger reservoir volume
No independent techno-economic analysis or system-code (ARIES/PROCESS equivalent) study of a levitated dipole power plant exists in the public literature
Top (levitation) magnet design and cost explicitly out of scope in Simpson et al. — paper assumes negligible cost without justification

Capital cost density high (~$15,000–20,000/kWe at 208 MWe net) because physics-sized large components (magnet, blanket, shield) are paired with modest net output squeezed by ~30% recirculating fraction
